<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par75" />{{center|V. ''In General.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|hh}}
17. In Aramaic the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} of all the conjugations terminate in {{GHGheb|text=־ֵא}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}. The Hebrew ''infinitives, imperatives'', and ''imperfects'' in {{GHGheb|text=־ֵה}}, less frequently {{GHGheb|text=־ֵא}} or {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}, may be due to imitation of these forms. On the ''infinitive construct Piʿēl'' {{GHGheb|text=חַכֵּי}}, see above, aa; {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=הֱוֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=37|verse=6}} (in the sense of ''fall''); {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵרֵא|translate=let him look out}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=33}} (but see above, p); {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲשֵׂה|translate=he will do}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תִּֽהְיֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תֹּבֵא|translate=consent thou not}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תַּֽעֲשֵׂה|translate=do thou not}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=12}} (the same form in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=16}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}); {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽהְיֵה}} (so Baer and Ginsburg, after cod. Hillel, &c.) ''I will be'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַנַּֽעֲשֵׂה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּרְאֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=13}}. Cf. also in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=יִמָּצֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּבָּנֵה}} (according to Qimḥi) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=27}}; in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּגַלֵּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=18|verse=7.8.12–17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=20|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, in each case {{GHGheb|text=לֹא תְגַלֵּה֑}}, beside {{GHGheb|text=תְּגַלֶּה}} with a minor distinctive; {{GHGheb|text=יֲנַקֵּ֑ה}} (Baer {{GHGheb|text=יְנַפֶּה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֱזָרֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=5|verse=12}} (with {{GHGterm|Zaqeph}}; Baer {{GHGheb|text=אֱזָרֶה}}). The fact, however, that a great number of these forms occur in {{GHGterm|pause}} and represent at the same time a {{GHGterm|jussive}} or ''voluntative'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=9}}), suggests the view that the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} is used merely to increase the emphasis of the pausal form, and at the same time to make a distinction in sound between the {{GHGterm|jussive}} or ''voluntative'' and the ordinary {{GHGterm|imperfect}}.<ref>Possibly these examples (like the eases of {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in {{GHGterm|pause}}, see n) represent the view of a particular Masoretic school, which was intended to be consistently carried out.</ref> Elsewhere ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=13}}; according to Baer also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=5}}) the pronunciation with ''ê'' is probably intended to soften the hiatus caused by a following {{GHGheb|text=א}} or {{GHGheb|text=ע}}; cf. the analogous cases above, {{GHGpar|74|l}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|ii}}
The ending {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} appears to stand for {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} in {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּזְנִי־שָׁם|translate=and there hath she played the harlot}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=6}}; perhaps, however, the 2nd ''sing. fem.'' is intended, or it may have been introduced into the text of Jeremiah from {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=15}}, &c. Still more strange is it in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תֶּ֑מְחִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=23}}; but the ''Mil‛ēl''-tone probably points to {{GHGheb|text=תֶּ֫מַח}} as the correct reading (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=14}}). The {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} stands for {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽחֱלִי|translate=he made sick}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=10}}, which is probably for {{GHGheb|text=החליא}} from {{GHGheb|text=חלא}}, a secondary form of {{GHGheb|text=חלה}}; see rr. The ''plur''. {{GHGheb|text=הִמְסִיו}} (Baer {{GHGheb|text=הִמְסִיוְ}}) ''they made to melt'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=14|verse=8}}, is a purely Aramaic form.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|kk}}
18. In two verbs the rare conjugation ''Pa‛lēl'' or its reflexive ({{GHGpar|55|d}}) occurs: {{GHGheb|text=מְטַֽחֲוֵי|translate=archers}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=16}} (from {{GHGheb|text=טָחָה}}); but most frequently in {{GHGheb|text=שָׁחָה|translate=to bend}}, ''Pa‛lēl'' {{GHGheb|text=שַֽׁחֲוָה}} not in use, whence reflexive {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁתַּֽחֲוָה|translate=to bow oneself, to prostrate oneself}}, 2nd ''pers.'' in {{GHGheb|text=־ִ֫ יתָ}} and 1st ''pers.'' in {{GHGheb|text=־ֵ֫ יתִי}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁתַּֽחֲוֶה}}, {{GHGterm|consecutive}} 3rd ''sing. masc.'' {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשְׁתַּ֫חוּ}} for ''wayyištaḥw'' (analogous to the noun-forms, like {{GHGheb|text=שָׂ֫חוּ}} for ''saḥw''); 3rd ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ}}.—Instead of the aramaizing {{GHGterm|infinitive}} with ''suffix'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּהִשְׁתַּֽחֲיָיָֽתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=18}} read with König {{GHGheb|text=בְּהִשְׁתַּֽחֲווֹתִי}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁתַּֽחֲוִיתֶם}} is still more certainly a scribal error for {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁתַּֽחֲוִים}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|ll}}
19. Before ''suffixes'' in all forms ending in {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, a connecting vowel is employed instead of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} and the connecting vowel which precedes it ({{GHGpar|58|f}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נָחַ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=27}}; in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=עָנָ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=30}}, &c., even with lesser disjunctives, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=22}}, or with a conjunctive accent, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=15}} (but Baer {{GHGheb|text=עָנַ֫נִי}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=19}}; cf. {{GHGpar|59|h}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָֽנְךָ֫}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=עָנָךְ}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=19}} (and even when not in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=37}}) or like {{GHGheb|text=קָנֶ֫ךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְיַרְבֶּ֑ךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְיַפְרְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=3}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עָנָ֫הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָנָם}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲנֵ֫הוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעַנְךָ֫|translate=Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִכַּ֫נִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֶלְךָ֫}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִכֶּ֫הוּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|mm}}
Only very seldom does the ''imperat.'' or {{GHGterm|impf.}} end in {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}} before suffixes, e.g.<section end="par75" /><noinclude>
